facts.text: AKO creates or updates connection secrets in the same namespace as the AtlasDatabaseUser resource. They contain connectionStringStandard, a standard SRV connection string, username and password, so applications running in Kubernetes can use them to connect. AKO reads the database user's password from an opaque Secret with a single password field, created in the same namespace as the AtlasDatabaseUser resource. AKO watches only secrets labelled atlas.mongodb.com/type=credentials. Terraform state and plan files can contain sensitive values such as initial database passwords.

19. Terraform's preview is `terraform plan` (refresh, then diff). 20. AKO's analogue is **Dry Run** (public preview). It runs the manager with `--dry-run` as a Kubernetes Job, or via `atlas kubernetes dry-run`. Continuous reconciliation is both a feature and a hazard. Feature: Stategraph presents drift detection that fixes drift rather than only reporting it as a benefit. Hazard: Encore says a continuously reconciling control plane (Crossplane) reverts emergency manual fixes unless reconciliation is paused first; the MongoDB Atlas Kubernetes Operator likewise undoes manual changes unless its reconciliation-policy=skip annotation is set. Runtime, not tool: tofu-controller is a Flux controller that reconciles Terraform and OpenTofu resources. Terraform does not revert drift by default: it offers -refresh-only mode, which updates state to match changes made outside Terraform, and HCP Terraform health assessments do not modify infrastructure. An out-of-band major-version upgrade of an Atlas cluster has also needed a Terraform provider fix, because the provider kept a stale mongo_db_major_version in state.
